title: The Nile without a Dragoman

history.note: A printer’s error corrected: “coutract” for “contract” (p. 3). A misreading corrected, a broken “l” read as “i”: “ali” for “all” (p. 125) (found by a sweep of all the books at the review after forty books).
A printer’s error corrected: “severely” for “severely.” (p. 271) (found by a sweep of all the books after a reader’s report (issue #117), checked on the scan).

Title page typed line by line as printed.

summary: Ordered south for his health in 1869, Frederic Eden and his wife spent the winter of 1869–70 on the Nile in the Lotus, a dahabeah hired from an acquaintance at Alexandria, and ran the voyage themselves instead of engaging a dragoman to do it for them. The book follows the journey from Alexandria by the canal and the Delta to Cairo, up the river by Minieh, Sioot, Keneh, Esné, and Assouan to Philæ, through Nubia to Wadi Halfeh, and back down by the cataract, Thebes, and Cairo. Alongside the temples, villages, and river life it gives practical detail for other travellers of modest means: the stores brought from England, with a list, prices in the markets, money, wages, and dealings with the reis and crew. The last page puts the whole cost from Cairo and back at £60 a month.
